The alpha-beta microstructure provides 45% higher specific strength than 4140 steel, critical for weight-sensitive designs. Its 6.7 W/mK thermal conductivity simplifies thermal management. This rationale is driven by laparoscopic stapler anvil plate and fat life requirements.
process: CNC swiss turning for surgical instruments geometry

commonFailures: Fatigue fracture at thread root under cyclic bending - resolved by thread rolling (not cutting) for compressive stress — critical for laparoscopic stapler anvil performance

faq.q: What specific material properties make Titanium Laparoscopic Stapler Anvil suitable for Laparoscopic stapler anvil plate?
faq.a: Titanium Laparoscopic Stapler Anvil uses Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V because its yield strength, fatigue endurance, and corrosion resistance directly address surgical instruments operational demands. The alloy's specific strength enables mass reduction without section compromise, while the TiO2 passivation ensures long-term environmental resistance.

faq.q: What are the critical dimensional tolerances for Titanium Laparoscopic Stapler Anvil?
faq.a: Standard machining tolerance for Titanium Laparoscopic Stapler Anvil is +/-0.05mm (ISO 2768-m). Functional mating surfaces are held to +/-0.025mm with Ra 0.8um finish, verified specifically for laparoscopic stapler anvil requirements. Threaded features conform to ISO 965-2 Class 6g, verified with calibrated Go/No-Go ring gauges on 100% of production.

faq.q: Does Titanium Laparoscopic Stapler Anvil require any post-machining surface treatment?
faq.a: Yes. laparoscopic stapler anvil components require Electropolishing + passivation per ASTM F86 (20-30% HNO3, 30min @50C) achieving Ra <0.2um for implant-grade finish — tailored for laparoscopic stapler anvil application. This restores the natural TiO2 passive layer removed during machining and provides the required surface properties for the specific service environment. Key parameters include surface finish Ra 0.8um and passive layer thickness verification per applicable standards.
